MovementMeasurementMode.Name: Movement Measurement
MovementMeasurementMode.Hint: Choose whether turn movement budgets are counted as scene distance or traversed grid fields.

DicePolicy.Name: Dice
DicePolicy.Hint: How rolls are made at this table. With physical dice, the roller rolls real dice and types in the result.

BonusActionShove.Name: Shove as a Bonus Action (Baldur's Gate 3)
BonusActionShove.Hint: An optional rule from Baldur's Gate 3. On: Shove (to knock Prone or push 5 feet) costs a Bonus Action instead of an Action. Off: it takes an Action, as in the 2024 rules.

HighGround.Name: High ground (Baldur's Gate 3)
HighGround.Hint: An optional rule from Baldur's Gate 3. On: an attack from 8 feet or more above its target gets +2 to its attack roll, and one from 8 feet or more below gets -2. Off: height gives no bonus, as in the 2024 rules.

BatchSaves.Name: Several saves at once
BatchSaves.Hint: When you roll saves for several creatures at once (a Fireball on your monsters): one window to type some and roll the rest, or every save rolled for you. One save is asked for on its own.

InspirationMonsterRerolls.Name: GM may reroll monster rolls with players' inspiration
InspirationMonsterRerolls.Hint: On: after a monster's d20 (an attack, a save or a check), the GM is asked whether to reroll it by spending a player character's Heroic Inspiration point. Off: only players spend their points, on their own failed rolls.

Core2014.Name: Offer 2014 core content
Core2014.Hint: Feats and subclasses from the 2014 core books in the level-up dialog.

Core2024.Name: Offer 2024 core content
Core2024.Hint: Feats and subclasses from the SRD and the 2024 core books in the level-up dialog.

Supplement.Name: Offer supplements
Supplement.Hint: Feats and subclasses from other official books (Tasha's, Xanathar's, ...) in the level-up dialog.

Ua.Name: Offer Unearthed Arcana
Ua.Hint: Playtest feats and subclasses in the level-up dialog.

ThirdParty.Name: Offer third-party and homebrew content
ThirdParty.Hint: Feats and subclasses from third-party books and homebrew compendiums in the level-up dialog.

RollHitPoints.Name: Roll hit points on level up
RollHitPoints.Hint: On: each level after the first rolls its Hit Die for hit points (at least 1, with the Fortitude modifier). Off: the Hit Die's average rounded up, as the 2024 rules suggest.

PlayersSeeOdds.Name: Players see the odds
PlayersSeeOdds.Hint: House rule. On: before acting, players see the chance to hit and the chance a target fails its save, which reveals targets' AC and save bonuses. Off: only the GM sees them, except against a creature whose defenses an effect has revealed to the player's creature.

RulesVersion.Name: Rules
RulesVersion.Hint: Which edition's conditions apply in this world: the 2024 rules, or the 2014 rules (Exhaustion's six levels, Grappled, Incapacitated, Invisible). Takes effect after a reload, for conditions applied from then on.

LANGUAGES.FontsHint: A font for a language its reader doesn't know, instead of its script, as language=font pairs (dwarvish=Dethek; elvish=Tengwar Annatar). Add the font files first, under Additional Fonts.

COVER.TotalRefused: That creature is behind Total Cover: it can't be targeted directly.

Summary.Prone: Your attacks have disadvantage. Attacks against you have advantage from within 5 ft, disadvantage from farther. Standing up costs half your Speed.
Summary.Blinded: You can't see. Your attacks have disadvantage; attacks against you have advantage.
Summary.Restrained: Speed 0. Your attacks and Agility saves have disadvantage; attacks against you have advantage.
Summary.Stunned: Incapacitated. You fail Might and Agility saves; attacks against you have advantage.
Summary.Unconscious: Incapacitated and Prone. You fail Might and Agility saves; attacks against you have advantage, and hits from within 5 ft are critical.
Summary.Exhaustion: Each level: −2 to d20 tests and −5 ft to every Speed. Level 6 is death.
Summary.Poisoned: Your attacks and ability checks have disadvantage.
Summary.Incapacitated: No actions, Bonus Actions or Reactions; your concentration ends. Disadvantage on initiative.
Summary.Paralyzed: Incapacitated, Speed 0. You fail Might and Agility saves; attacks against you have advantage, and hits from within 5 ft are critical.
Summary.Petrified: Turned to stone: Incapacitated, Speed 0, resistance to all damage, immune to Poisoned. You fail Might and Agility saves; attacks against you have advantage.
Summary.Invisible: Your attacks have advantage; attacks against you have disadvantage. Advantage on initiative.
Summary.Frightened: Your attacks and ability checks have disadvantage while the source of your fear is in sight.
Summary.Grappled: Speed 0. Your attacks against anyone but the grappler have disadvantage.
Summary.Charmed: You can't attack or harm the charmer.
Summary.Envenomed: Poison damage at the start of each of your turns, more with each stack.
Summary.Bleeding: Bleeding damage at the start of each of your turns.
Summary.Stunned2014: Incapacitated, Speed 0. You fail Might and Agility saves; attacks against you have advantage.
Summary.Exhaustion2014: Level 1: disadvantage on checks. 2: half Speed. 3: disadvantage on attacks and saves. 4: half Hit Point maximum. 5: Speed 0. 6: death.
